senses.gloss:
Yayāti
------------------------------------------
Yayāti has become famous in Vedāntic literature for his statement that desires can never be quenched by trying to satisfy them (vide महाभारत, Ādiparva, 85.12).
He was a king of the चन्द्रवṁश (lunar race), the son of another celebrated king नहुष, and queen Virajā. He had two wives, Devayānī and Śarmiṣṭhā. Anu, यदु, Turvasu, Druhyu and पूरु were his five sons.
Once, due to the curse of the sage शुक्राचार्य, ययाति lost his youth and became old. However the sage had also given him the boon that he could exchange his old-age with the youth of a young man. When ययाति requested his sons to exchange their youth, all refused except पूरु. After enjoying all the pleasures of life for many years ययाति found out the truth that lust could never be satiated by enjoyment. He then gave back the youth to prince पूरु, crowned him as the king and left for तपस्.
